subject: Problematic behavior of the optimizer in RStan

messages.author: 15d2d8f2bea2690f
messages.subject: Problematic behavior of the optimizer in RStan
parts:
Hi all,

I have used RStan's optimize function several times before without problems. However, I recently tried it on a new model and the optimizer is behaving strangely; it is giving me positive log probabilities. The log probability must be at most 0, as log(1)=0. The starting log probability is negative, but it increases beyond zero rather quickly. The algorithm still converges to a maximum, but I don't know whether it should be trusted. I can post the specific model if anyone wants to replicate the error, but I was just wondering whether this had happened to anyone before, or if anyone knows what the cause for this behavior could be.

Luis

It is only proportional to a log probability (i.e. it is unnormalized). A negative lp__ is common.

Ben

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Problematic behavior of the optimizer in RStan
parts:
The log probability refers to a log probability _density_,
not a proper probability (which requires integrating a
density over a finite neighborhood).  Probability densities
just have to be positive, in which case their log can take
on any value between -infty and infty.
